trigger: Google Play Protect operationalization and PHA detection reporting
observable_decision_or_change: Google Play Protect identifies potentially harmful apps; 2017 report attributes a share of PHA detections to machine-learning models.
complementors_affected: Android app developers whose apps are scanned or classified as safe/harmful/potentially harmful
primary_source_location: Google Play Protect / PHA detection sections

trigger: Privacy-sensitive SMS and Call Log permission abuse risk
observable_decision_or_change: Google Play restricted SMS and Call Log permissions and began removing violating apps.
complementors_affected: Developers requesting SMS or Call Log permissions outside allowed use cases

trigger: Bad apps, impersonation, inappropriate content, and PHAs
observable_decision_or_change: Google applied advanced machine-learning models, analyses, user engagement/feedback data, and human review to spot suspicious apps.
complementors_affected: Developers whose apps were suspicious, rejected, removed, or reviewed
primary_source_location: Harmful app contents and behaviors section

trigger: Policy-violating app submissions and malicious actors
observable_decision_or_change: Google enhanced ML detection systems analyzing code, metadata, and user engagement signals; improved vetting stopped more than 790,000 policy-violating submissions.
complementors_affected: Developers submitting apps to Google Play
primary_source_location: Main body, bullet list and preceding paragraph

trigger: Google Play publishing-format and Android 11 compatibility requirements
observable_decision_or_change: New apps required Android App Bundle and target API 30 in August 2021; updates required target API 30 in November 2021.
complementors_affected: Developers submitting new apps or updates on Google Play
primary_source_location: Requirements for new apps and updates sections

trigger: Need for app data-practice transparency before install
observable_decision_or_change: All Google Play apps must provide Data safety information; missing or unapproved sections can lead to rejection of new submissions or updates.
complementors_affected: All Google Play app developers
primary_source_location: Policy changes and What you can expect sections

trigger: Security and privacy risks around AccessibilityService API
observable_decision_or_change: Apps using AccessibilityService API must disclose data access/purpose in Play Console and get approval.
complementors_affected: Developers using AccessibilityService API

trigger: Need for developers to detect abuse and app/device integrity
observable_decision_or_change: Play Integrity API announced to let developers determine if requests come from genuine app binaries and genuine Android devices.
complementors_affected: Developers integrating anti-abuse integrity checks
primary_source_location: Protecting both you and our users section

trigger: Need for SDK transparency and policy/safety information
observable_decision_or_change: Google launched Google Play SDK Index with usage data and SDK insights for developers.
complementors_affected: App developers choosing, keeping, or removing commercial SDKs; SDK providers

trigger: Coordinated attacks on app ratings and review integrity
observable_decision_or_change: Google strengthened anomaly detection/investigation for suspicious review activity and introduced mandatory 24-hour delay for incoming app reviews.
complementors_affected: Developers affected by app ratings and reviews
primary_source_location: App reviews and policy support sections

trigger: Need for user control over account and in-app data
observable_decision_or_change: Developers with apps enabling account creation must provide in-app and web paths for account/data deletion linked in the Data safety form.
complementors_affected: Developers whose apps support account creation

trigger: Need to verify developers and reduce malware/fraud
observable_decision_or_change: Expanded Play Console developer verification requirements, including D-U-N-S numbers for organizations.
complementors_affected: New and existing Play Console developer accounts
primary_source_location: Requiring organizations to provide a D-U-N-S number section

trigger: Need for clearer policy compliance and SDK-related policy issue visibility
observable_decision_or_change: Google announced SDK-related policy issues in Policy status page and launched Play Strike Removal program for eligible developers after training.
complementors_affected: Developers with SDK-related policy issues or enforcement strikes
primary_source_location: Giving you a better policy experience section

trigger: App quality and fraud/malware prevention for new personal accounts
observable_decision_or_change: New personal developer accounts must test apps before publication, according to updated Google Play quality policy.
complementors_affected: New personal developer accounts
primary_source_location: Required app testing for all new personal developer accounts section

trigger: Unauthorized access, fraud, bots, cheating, data theft, and malware/device risk
observable_decision_or_change: Play Integrity API added app access risk, Play Protect verdict, recent device activity, and hardware-backed signal features.
complementors_affected: Developers using Play Integrity API to respond to abuse

trigger: Emerging risks from apps featuring generative AI content
observable_decision_or_change: Apps with generative AI must prohibit/prevent restricted content, provide in-app reporting/flagging, test models, and may be rejected or removed if ads or app behavior violate policy.
complementors_affected: Developers of apps featuring generative AI content

trigger: Potentially harmful app detection on devices
observable_decision_or_change: Google Play Protect scans apps daily and may disable particularly dangerous apps; Play Protect docs link this protection to machine learning and classification inputs.
complementors_affected: Developers of apps identified as harmful or potentially harmful

trigger: Bad actors and policy-violating app submissions
observable_decision_or_change: Google reports AI-powered threat detection and other security measures prevented 2.36 million policy-violating apps from being published on Google Play.
complementors_affected: Developers submitting apps to Google Play

trigger: Malware from internet-sideloaded sources and impersonation risks
observable_decision_or_change: Google announced developer verification for apps installed on certified Android devices, rolling out after 2025.
complementors_affected: Developers distributing apps to certified Android devices beyond Google Play

trigger: Developer requests for clearer compliance and fewer review surprises
observable_decision_or_change: Google rolled out Play Policy Insights in Android Studio and expanded Play Console pre-review checks.
complementors_affected: Developers preparing app submissions
primary_source_location: Simpler ways to build safer apps from the start section

trigger: COVID-19 health and safety information credibility concerns
observable_decision_or_change: Only recognized entities should submit COVID-19 related apps; apps are critically evaluated for reputable data sources.
complementors_affected: Developers submitting COVID-19 apps

trigger: Need for App Store privacy disclosure before download
observable_decision_or_change: App privacy information required to submit new apps and app updates starting December 8, 2020.
complementors_affected: App Store developers submitting new apps or updates

trigger: Cross-app tracking and advertising identifier access
observable_decision_or_change: All apps must use AppTrackingTransparency to request permission to track users or access the advertising identifier.
complementors_affected: Developers whose apps track users or access advertising identifiers

trigger: Fraudulent apps, bait-and-switch behavior, privacy violations
observable_decision_or_change: Apps discovered switching functionality are rejected or removed; developers are notified of a 14-day appeals process before permanent account termination.
complementors_affected: Developers whose apps are rejected, removed, or whose accounts face termination

trigger: User control over account and personal data deletion
observable_decision_or_change: Apps that support account creation must allow users to initiate account deletion within the app.
complementors_affected: Developers whose apps support account creation

trigger: Fingerprinting risk from APIs that can identify devices/users
observable_decision_or_change: Developers must declare approved reasons for certain APIs in privacy manifests; uploads receive notice if reasons are missing.
complementors_affected: Developers using APIs that require reasons, including through SDKs

trigger: Third-party SDK privacy and required reason API enforcement
observable_decision_or_change: Apple sends missing-reason notices from March 13 and requires approved reasons for relevant APIs to upload apps from May 1.
complementors_affected: Developers uploading apps or updates with listed APIs or commonly used third-party SDKs
primary_source_location: Starting March 13 and Starting May 1 sections

trigger: Android requirements for Fire OS 6 and Fire OS 7
observable_decision_or_change: Amazon release notes state it will enforce minimum API level requirements for Fire OS 6 and Fire OS 7.
complementors_affected: Amazon Appstore developers targeting Fire OS 6/7

trigger: App submission format support change
observable_decision_or_change: Amazon Appstore supports uploading apps in Android App Bundles format.
complementors_affected: Developers submitting apps to Amazon Appstore

trigger: Need for user-data privacy transparency in Amazon Appstore
observable_decision_or_change: Amazon introduced privacy labels, opened questionnaire in Developer Console, required compliance before November 2, and displays 'Information not provided by developer' for pending questionnaires.
complementors_affected: Amazon Appstore developers
primary_source_location: Introducing Appstore privacy labels and FAQ sections

trigger: Amazon Appstore Android-device program change
observable_decision_or_change: Amazon discontinued support for Amazon Appstore on Android devices; new Android-targeting submissions stop February 20 and updates continue until August 20, 2025.
complementors_affected: Developers targeting non-Amazon Android devices through Amazon Appstore

trigger: Vega OS binary submission support for Fire TV devices
observable_decision_or_change: Amazon Appstore release notes state VPKG binary submissions are supported for Fire TV devices running Vega OS.
complementors_affected: Developers targeting Vega OS Fire TV devices
